cards.text: Jesus and the people traveling with Him are on the road again, and He comes into a village. Somebody there is about to welcome Him in. Me? The last trip I took was across a kitchen and into a junk drawer. One way. No return ticket.

cards.question: In this village, a woman named Martha welcomes Jesus into her ___.

cards.text: Martha has a sister named Mary. And while the whole house is buzzing, Mary heads straight for the guest of honor.

cards.question: Martha's sister Mary finds a spot near Jesus. What does she do there?

answers.text: Sits at His feet listening to Him
Brings Him a bowl of fresh water
Asks Him to bless the whole house

cards.text: But Martha is distracted by all the preparations to be made. I KNOW that look, friend. That's me with four timers going off at once and my apron on backwards.

cards.question: Martha comes to Jesus and asks if He doesn't care about something. What is it?

answers.text: That her sister left her to serve alone
That the house is too small for everyone
That His followers came without warning

cards.question: True or false: Martha asks Jesus to tell Mary to help her.

cards.text: "Martha, Martha," the Lord replies. When somebody says your name TWICE, you put down whatever you're holding. Spoon, dish towel, everything. Down.

cards.question: True or false: Jesus tells Martha she is worried and upset about many things.

cards.text: Then Jesus tells Martha how much is REALLY needed. Friend, I'm in no position to talk. A neighbor once stopped by just to say hi, and I stamped a cookie TOWER.

cards.question: Jesus tells Martha that only ___ thing is necessary.
Jesus says Mary has chosen the good portion. What does He say about it?

answers.text: It will not be taken away from her
She has to set it aside for now
She can have it once the work is done

cards.question: True or false: Jesus sends Mary off to help Martha with the preparations.

findings.problem: The opening card has six sentences: the setup sentence, 'Somebody there is about to welcome Him in.', 'Me?', 'The last trip I took was across a kitchen and into a junk drawer.', 'One way.' and 'No return ticket.' The limit is three.

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on.

findings.problem: The joke calls the move into the junk drawer his last trip, with 'One way. No return ticket.' That contradicts his backstory. The angel took him out of the drawer and into the Dorinverse, so the drawer was not his last trip and it was not one way.

rule.text: His own world isn't Bible fact. His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them. His jokes can make up small moments and habits around his bakery.

findings.problem: The joke has a neighbor stopping by while Papa Dorin stamps a cookie tower. In the backstory he lives alone on a planet just big enough for his bakery, so he has no neighbors there. In the Millers' kitchen, Mother Miller did the stamping, not Dorin. Either way, the joke adds something new to his world that is outside small moments and habits around his bakery.

rule.text: His own world isn't Bible fact. His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them. His jokes can make up small moments and habits around his bakery.

findings.problem: 'Jesus tells Martha how much is REALLY needed' presents 'only one thing is necessary' as a statement about how many preparations are needed. The cookie-tower joke backs up that reading. The text does not say what the one thing is or how it connects to the preparations, so the card fills in something the text leaves open.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The card cites only Luke 10:39, but 'while the whole house is buzzing' draws on the preparations in Luke 10:40. 'Heads straight for the guest of honor' also adds a movement the text doesn't describe. Luke 10:39 only says Mary sat at the Lord's feet.

rule.text: Cite exactly what the card uses. Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.
